The invention relates to a method for transferring unit loads (6-1, 6-2) into storage channels (15) for storage. The unit loads are conveyed to the storage channels by means of a unit load receiving device (7), which is movable along the storage channels in an x-direction, and by means of a transport device (28), which is extendable into the storage channel in a z-direction. outputs.L2: The invention concerns a process for placing unit loads (6-1, 6-2) into storage channels (15). The unit loads are delivered to the storage channels by a unit-load receiving device (7), which can travel along the storage channels in the x-direction, and by a transport device (28), which is extendable into a storage channel in the z-direction. The transport device includes outer transport elements (64, 65) arranged at opposite end regions and may also include an intermediate inner transport element (66). outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a method for transferring unit loads into storage channels for storage, particularly in an automated storage system. In this method, the unit loads are handled by a receiving device that can travel along the storage channels in a first direction, referred to as the x-direction. The receiving device is positioned in front of a selected storage channel in order to introduce a unit load into that channel.

For moving the unit load into the storage channel, the system uses a transport device that can extend into the storage channel in a second direction, referred to as the z-direction. The transport device is arranged on or associated with the receiving device and is designed to move the unit load from the receiving device into the storage channel. The transport device comprises transport elements that act on the unit load and displace it in the z-direction. In particular, the transport device includes outer transport elements arranged at opposite ends. In some embodiments, an additional inner transport element may be arranged between the outer transport elements.

During operation, a unit load is initially located on the receiving device. After the receiving device has been aligned with the desired storage channel, one of the transport elements of the transport device moves the unit load from the receiving device into the storage channel. This first movement transfers the unit load only part of the way into the storage channel, placing it in an intermediate position within the channel.

After the unit load has reached this intermediate position, the transport device is repositioned relative to the unit load and/or relative to the storage channel. This repositioning makes it possible for another transport element of the transport device to engage the unit load. The further transport element then pushes the unit load from the intermediate position farther into the storage channel until the unit load reaches a deeper final storage position.

In this way, the unit load can be transferred step by step into the storage channel. By using different transport elements for successive movement stages, the system can place the unit load deeper within the storage channel than would be possible with a single pushing movement alone. The method therefore enables efficient storage of unit loads in storage channels, including storage positions located at greater depths within the channel.
outputs.L4:
A method is provided for transferring unit loads, such as pallets, containers, trays, or similar goods carriers, into storage channels of a storage system. The method uses a movable receiving device, for example a shuttle, carriage, lift platform, or other load-handling unit, which can be positioned in front of a selected storage channel. Mounted on, or operatively associated with, the receiving device is an extendable transport device designed to move a unit load from the receiving device into the storage channel.

The transport device includes a plurality of transport elements arranged one behind another in the direction of movement of the unit load. These transport elements may be formed as pushers, drivers, conveying fingers, chains, belts, telescopic members, or other movable engagement members. During the storage operation, the transport elements do not necessarily act on the load all at once. Instead, they engage the unit load sequentially so that the load can be advanced step by step into the storage channel.

In a first phase of the method, the receiving device is brought into alignment with the selected storage channel. A unit load supported on the receiving device is then engaged by a first transport element of the extendable transport device. By extending or actuating the transport device, the first transport element pushes or otherwise moves the unit load from the receiving device into the entrance region of the storage channel. The unit load is thereby transferred to an intermediate storage position within the channel. This intermediate position may correspond to a first storage depth or to a position from which the load can be further advanced.

After the unit load has reached the intermediate position, the transport device is repositioned or further extended so that another transport element can engage the unit load from behind. In particular, a second transport element, located farther back in relation to the direction of insertion, is brought into contact with the rear side of the unit load. This second engagement allows the unit load to be shifted farther into the storage channel without requiring the receiving device itself to enter the channel.

In a subsequent phase, the second transport element advances the unit load from the intermediate position to a deeper storage position. If required, additional transport elements may engage the load in succession, each moving the load farther into the channel. In this way, the load can be placed at a second, third, or further storage depth depending on the configuration of the storage channel and the desired storage location.

The method therefore enables controlled multi-depth placement of unit loads in a storage channel. By moving the load first into an intermediate position and then re-engaging it from behind for further advancement, the system can store loads at different depths using a compact receiving device and an extendable transport mechanism. This reduces the need for long or complex load-handling equipment, while still allowing accurate positioning of unit loads deep within storage channels.

The described approach is particularly suitable for high-density storage systems in which several unit loads are arranged one behind another in a channel. It allows the receiving device to remain outside or substantially outside the storage channel while the extendable transport device performs the insertion movement. The sequential engagement of the load by multiple transport elements improves control over the transfer process and helps ensure reliable positioning of the unit load at the intended storage location.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article because it points to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. When we say “the book,” we are not talking about just any book—we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

Although “the” may seem simple, it helps make sentences clearer and more precise. For example, “I saw a dog” introduces any dog, while “I saw the dog” suggests a specific dog already known in the conversation. This small difference can change the meaning of a sentence.

The word “the” also appears in many titles, names, and expressions, such as “The United States,” “The Great Wall,” and “the best.” It gives importance and identity to the nouns it introduces.

In everyday language, “the” is easy to overlook because it is used so often. However, without it, English would sound incomplete and less natural. This tiny word shows that even the simplest parts of language can have great value.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a method of transferring unit loads into storage channels using a movable receiving device and an extendable transport device with outer and optional inner transport elements.
counterfactuals.output: A method for transferring unit loads into storage channels of a storage system includes positioning a movable receiving device adjacent to a selected storage channel and receiving at least one unit load on the receiving device. An extendable transport device associated with the receiving device is extended in a transfer direction toward or into the storage channel. The transport device includes outer transport elements configured to support and convey the unit load, and optionally inner transport elements movable relative to the outer transport elements. The unit load is advanced from the receiving device into the storage channel by driving the outer transport elements and, when provided, by extending and/or driving the inner transport elements to increase the effective transfer reach. After placement of the unit load at a predetermined storage position within the storage channel, the transport device is retracted to the receiving device. The method enables controlled deposition of unit loads in storage channels while reducing the required movement of the receiving device and permitting transfer into channels of different depths.

counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Relates To

The invention relates generally to storage and retrieval systems for unit loads, such as pallets, trays, containers, or other load carriers, and more particularly to shuttle-based automated storage systems having storage channels configured to receive multiple unit loads in a depth direction.

The invention further relates to a method and apparatus for placing a unit load into a deep storage channel using a shuttle vehicle or shuttle device that is movable along an aisle or transfer path and that includes a load-handling mechanism for pushing or otherwise advancing the unit load into the storage channel.

In particular, the invention relates to a storage process in which the shuttle initially advances the unit load from an entry side of the storage channel to an intermediate position within the channel, thereafter retracts or repositions at least a portion of the shuttle or its load-handling mechanism, and subsequently advances the unit load farther into the storage channel to a deeper storage position. By performing the placement operation in multiple pushing stages, the shuttle may store unit loads at depths greater than the effective stroke or reach of a single push operation, while avoiding the need for an excessively long pusher, telescopic mechanism, or shuttle body.

The invention is applicable to automated warehouses, pallet shuttle systems, high-density storage racks, deep-lane storage systems, buffer storage installations, and other material-handling arrangements in which unit loads are stored in channels, lanes, bays, or compartments extending inwardly from an access aisle.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.output: An automated storage system handles a load using an extendable z-direction transport device positioned at a receiving device adjacent to a storage channel. In a first stage, the transport device extends a first transport element to engage and transfer the load from the receiving device into an intermediate position within the storage channel. In a second stage, a different transport element of the same z-direction transport device is actuated to engage the load and move it farther into the storage channel to its final storage position. The staged transfer allows deep placement of the load in the channel while limiting the required stroke or configuration of any single transport element.
